QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_46

question.text: The SE planted 10,000 mangrove seedlings. Under SAS-500, why are MANGROVE plantations given a higher SROI coefficient than upland plantations?

answer.text: Mangroves combine carbon sequestration + storm-surge / coastal protection + fisheries nursery + high per-hectare biomass — so the monetised ecosystem service per hectare is higher (blue-carbon economics)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Mangrove ('blue carbon') ecosystems provide stacked services: carbon, coastal protection, fisheries. Per-hectare monetary valuation is higher than upland forest. SAS-500 SROI uses stacked ecosystem-service valuation. **The Trap:** Options B, C, D are trivial or wrong. **Cross-Exam Context:** Blue-carbon economics also in XV Research Analyst ESG themes and BRSR Compliance (III-A / III-C). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Cite the ecosystem-service valuation source clearly (e.g., TEEB India, MoEF&CC Green-Accounts) — reviewers challenge SROI coefficients when the source is unnamed.
